mission_result: Implemented and verified an executable multi-stage continuation canary. A worker can keep same-context/same-authority checkpoints in one run, consume proven successor readiness, attempt an exclusive create-if-absent successor claim, allow only the winner to start the successor run, and leave independent sibling successor paths parallel. Context/authority changes or an existing claim force allocator re-entry instead of unsafe continuation.
negative_knowledge: Sequential continuation must not become a global worker lock; exclusivity is per successor claim path only.
Derived readiness is consumed only when durable proof refs exist and failed/conflicted prerequisites are empty; this module does not replace the separate readiness owner.
Winning an opportunity claim grants only the successor opportunity's scoped candidate authority, never Current/Human Accepted/Served authority.
A context or authority change is a split/boundary signal, not a reason to silently drag the prior run's permissions forward.
remaining_boundary: Live integration into the separately owned role-fluid allocator and dynamic-readiness implementation should occur after those owners return/reconcile. This run deliberately avoided concurrent edits to their files. Remote GitHub/other transports must preserve CREATE_IF_ABSENT_EXCLUSIVE semantics; this candidate does not promote production /w.

next_work.action: Consume this continuation receipt after their returns so post-return allocation can call the same atomic successor contract without duplicating readiness or allocator ownership.
